record_body:
Account summary
- Existing Redwood Hosted API customer (primary region: eu-west; secondary: us-east). Uses chat + retrieval-augmented responses in BrightDesk agent console.
- Current sentiment: positive on quality + developer experience, but they escalated on p95 latency in eu-west previously. They keep asking, “how will you catch this before we do?”

Firmographics / environment
- Product: customer support platform (agent assist + auto-summaries).
- Deployment preference: VPC-required for production inference (private networking + egress control). They are okay starting Hosted API for pilot features but want Dedicated/VPC for core workflows.
- Compliance: SOC2 required; SSO/SAML for admin console; audit logs + retention controls. Strong preference for EU data residency for EU tenants.

Workload & requirements (as captured by SE/CSM)
- Workload types: 
  - real-time agent assist (streaming chat)
  - ticket summarization (non-streaming, batchy)
  - doc-search embeddings (periodic re-index)
- Latency targets:
  - streaming: first token p95 < 600ms in eu-west, stable under peak concurrency
  - non-streaming: end-to-end p95 < 3.5s for typical summaries
- Throughput concerns:
  - reported “tokens/sec feels bursty” during peak hours; wants predictable throughput and clearer throttling behavior
- Operational asks:
  - proactive regression alerts tied to deploys (runtime/model updates)
  - “what changed?” context: runtime build/SHA, GPU type, scheduler changes, region

Notable history / escalations
- SUP-18421 (eu-west p95 spike):
  - Customer reported elevated p95 latency on a single chat route.
  - Internal notes: correlated with runtime deploy window + fleet heterogeneity. Customer asked for earlier warning/rollback.
- SUP-18444 (tokens/sec drop after model version update):
  - Customer observed throughput drop in production after they switched to a new pinned model version.
  - Follow-up: they want Redwood to provide regression detection signals and guidance on “safe rollouts” for model/runtime changes.

Recent activity timeline
- 2026-02-03: shared a recording + notes from a latency monitoring deep dive (Fireflies: ff_2026-02-03_enterprise-tech-deep-dive-latency-monitoring). Customer question: “do you have canaries in prod or is it all offline benchmarking?”
- 2026-02-07: CSM follow-up: provided short write-up on current observability (per-route p95, tokens/sec) + limitations. Customer requested roadmap for regression detection.
- 2026-02-12: internal alignment w/ SRE on how to message the new perf regression canary program (link: sean_gallagher/thread_2b61d8f4c90a). Goal: avoid overpromising (“internal detection v1”).
- 2026-02-18: evaluation call (BrightDesk Eng + Platform): asked specifically for:
  - deploy annotations on dashboards
  - paging/incident workflow: “who sees it first, and what’s the rollback plan?”
  - ability to slice by GPU SKU + runtime build when there’s a regression

Open notes (CRM-style)
- They’re not asking for a formal external SLA feature yet, but they want proof that we can detect regressions before they cause a customer-visible incident.
- Quote (paraphrase): “We can’t be your monitoring system. If p95 shifts, we need you to catch it and tell us what changed.”
- Strong interest in Dedicated (eu-west) for predictable performance; they’ll accept staged rollout if we can show: (a) stable p95 time-series, (b) clear alerts with context, (c) maintenance window suppression during deploys.

Proposed plan (for next call)
- Walk through internal perf regression canary approach (p95 + tokens/sec per model/region slices) and show sample dashboard + alert payload structure.
- Offer: Dedicated pilot in eu-west with guardrails:
  - pinned runtime build during pilot
  - deploy annotations + rollback runbook
  - weekly performance review (p95 + tokens/sec) and threshold tuning

Internal-only reminders
- Keep wording careful: perf-canary is internal detection/operational readiness v1 (not a customer-facing SLA product).
- If they request access to perf-canary dashboards: confirm what we can safely share vs internal-only namespaces; route through least-privilege access process.
